meta.source: The VIA Classification of Character Strengths and Virtues (VIA Institute on Character; originating research by Christopher Peterson and Martin Seligman, Character Strengths and Virtues: A Handbook and Classification, 2004)
meta.license_note: (c) VIA Institute on Character, all rights reserved; VIA is a registered trademark. VIA Institute's own mission is free dissemination of this classification for education and research, and its VIA Survey is openly available, but the text itself is still copyrighted. The six virtue names and 24 strength names are VIA's own; every paraphrase here is written for this project, never VIA's own first-person survey-style text.
meta.scope_note: VIA's classification is a general character-strengths taxonomy, not a CS-specific or even SEL-specific one. Unlike CASEL/CDE's T-SEL/RULER, which group skills by emotional or social competency, VIA groups strengths by classical virtue, and everyone is understood to carry all 24 strengths to some degree rather than mastering them in sequence. Teamwork, Leadership, Perseverance, Judgment, and Creativity read as likely strong candidates for a future carrier alignment pass against this project's existing Kagan/ROV Robotics content.
meta.codes_note: Codes are this project's own sequential numbering per virtue (<virtue-abbreviation>.<n>), not an official VIA scheme -- VIA names its 24 strengths but doesn't number them.

groups.name: Wisdom
groups.paraphrase: Strengths that involve acquiring and using knowledge well.

items.name: Creativity
items.paraphrase: Coming up with ideas that are both original and genuinely useful, not just different for its own sake.

items.name: Curiosity
items.paraphrase: Actively seeking out new experiences and information rather than waiting for them to show up.

items.name: Judgment
items.paraphrase: Weighing a decision from multiple angles, including evidence that cuts against what you already believe.

items.name: Love of Learning
items.paraphrase: Being motivated to build real depth in a subject or skill, not just to get through it.

items.name: Perspective
items.paraphrase: Being the person others come to for advice because you can see the bigger picture, drawing on your own experience to help someone else see it too.

groups.name: Courage
groups.paraphrase: Strengths that involve exercising will to accomplish goals in the face of difficulty.

items.name: Bravery
items.paraphrase: Acting on what you believe is right even when it's risky, difficult, or frightening.

items.name: Honesty
items.paraphrase: Presenting yourself accurately to other people and taking responsibility for your own actions.

items.name: Perseverance
items.paraphrase: Continuing to work toward a goal despite obstacles or setbacks.

items.name: Zest
items.paraphrase: Approaching life with energy and enthusiasm rather than going through the motions.

groups.name: Humanity
groups.paraphrase: Strengths that show up in caring for and befriending other people.

items.name: Kindness
items.paraphrase: Doing something genuinely helpful for someone else without expecting anything back.

items.name: Love
items.paraphrase: Building close relationships defined by mutual care, not just shared proximity.

items.name: Social Intelligence
items.paraphrase: Being aware of your own feelings and reading what the people around you are feeling too.

groups.name: Justice
groups.paraphrase: Strengths that underlie a healthy community life.

items.name: Fairness
items.paraphrase: Treating people equally and applying the same rules to everyone, not just the people you favor.

items.name: Leadership
items.paraphrase: Guiding a group toward a shared goal while keeping relationships among its members healthy.

items.name: Teamwork
items.paraphrase: Contributing your share to a group's effort and feeling responsible for the team's success, not just your own part.

items.name: Forgiveness
items.paraphrase: Letting go of resentment toward someone who wronged you, without pretending it didn't happen.

items.name: Humility
items.paraphrase: Knowing your own strengths without needing to be the center of attention for them.

items.name: Prudence
items.paraphrase: Thinking ahead and avoiding unnecessary risk rather than acting on impulse.

items.name: Self-Regulation
items.paraphrase: Managing your own impulses and actions on purpose, rather than being managed by them.

groups.name: Transcendence
groups.paraphrase: Strengths that forge connections to the larger universe and provide meaning.

items.name: Appreciation of Beauty and Excellence
items.paraphrase: Noticing and genuinely responding to something well made or well done, whether it's art, nature, or someone else's skill.

items.name: Gratitude
items.paraphrase: Noticing when someone has helped you and actually telling them so.

items.name: Hope
items.paraphrase: Staying realistic about a situation while still expecting things to work out.

items.name: Humor
items.paraphrase: Finding something to laugh about, including in a stressful moment, without making it at someone else's expense.

items.name: Spirituality
items.paraphrase: Having a sense that your life fits into something larger than yourself.
